sections.h2: How can a Jacksonville homeowner sell fast?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, accept a cash offer, or hand the house over untouched to an as-is purchaser who absorbs the repair bill. Whichever you choose, two witnesses sign the deed and the Duval County clerk records it. How quickly it all happens depends on the buyer's financing, the state of title and any lien that needs a payoff letter.

The city is huge and varied, which means the best route changes house by house. A tidy house in a popular area can do well in a standard listing. A house needing a roof, rewiring or storm repair, or one tied up by tenants or an estate, often suits a cash or as-is buyer because no lender inspection stands in the way.

  • Listing: biggest buyer pool, longest timeline, lender appraisal and repair requests.
  • Cash or as-is: fewer conditions, and you price the condition in.
  • Family transfer: still a conveyance for value, and the homestead rules below still apply.

Jacksonville and Duval County merged governments in 1968, and the city calls itself the largest city by area in the continental United States, with 747.29 land square miles. Population is estimated at 1,017,689 for July 2025. One municipal government covers beach communities, a riverfront downtown, suburban subdivisions and rural edges, so conditions differ block by block and a neighbor's experience may not match yours.

The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $293,700, owners occupy 57.6 percent of homes, and the middle rent is $1,465. Permit, utility and code questions all go to the same city, which makes it the place to ask about open permits on your property before you list.

sections.h2: How Duval's homestead exemption plays into a sale
sections.html:
Your exemption ends with the sale and the buyer files their own. The Duval County Property Appraiser describes a $25,000 exemption, plus up to $25,000 more on value above $50,000 that skips school taxes.

When a home sells, assessed value goes up to market value for the next tax roll, and the Save Our Homes ceiling of 3 percent or less on yearly increases begins again for the new owner. A buyer who held a Florida homestead in any of the three prior roll years can file for portability, a separate application. The timely date for both is March 1, and late filing runs to early September.

Duval renews exemptions automatically each January 1 when nothing has changed, and a renewal card arrives as a receipt. The office also has a brochure on how short-term renting can affect exemptions, which landlords should read before listing a house they once lived in. For forms, call 904-255-5900 or email pacustserv@coj.net. The office is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260.

sections.h2: Other exemptions a buyer or seller might mention
sections.html:
The Duval appraiser offers many categories beyond the basic homestead, and a buyer's ability to claim them can shape an offer. Ask the office whether a benefit survives or must be refiled after your sale.

  • Military and service members: armed forces deployment, disabled veteran, and service-connected total and permanent disability exemptions.
  • First responders: a total and permanent disability exemption for them and their surviving spouses, and a homestead exemption for surviving spouses of military personnel or first responders.
  • Seniors: a senior citizen exemption with its own application and the Duval 501 form.
  • Other: blindness, widow or widower, disability, a granny-flat assessment reduction for parents' or grandparents' quarters, conservation land, and institutional or non-profit exemptions.
  • Historic preservation: available through the City of Jacksonville.

Several forms are handed out by phone or email, so call 904-255-5900 to make sure you hold the current version.

sections.h2: Where the sale proceeds from here
sections.html:
Start with the two offices you will lean on most. The Duval County Property Appraiser answers exemption and portability questions, and the Duval tax collector gives you the balance due. The city itself handles permits, utilities and code questions, so one call there can show whether any work on the house is still open.

Next, decide how you want to sell. A tidy house in a sought-after area may net more through an agent, though showings and a lender's appraisal slow the schedule. A house with a worn roof, tenants or a tangled estate often moves quicker to a buyer who pays cash and accepts it as is. Whatever the route, collect offers in writing, compare the amount you keep rather than the headline price, and confirm who pays recording and deed tax before you sign.

Duval follows the standard state deed rate of 70 cents for each $100 paid, and all signers share liability. A mortgage on the property counts as consideration whether or not the buyer assumes it.

Payment goes to the clerk at the recording counter. Recording fees under section 28.24 begin at $5.00 for a first page and rise with extra pages, names and technology charges.

On the property tax side, value is set January 1, bills come in November, discounts shrink month by month into February, and unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1. The title agent prorates the year at closing. Ask the Duval tax collector for your balance instead of estimating.

sections.h2: Foreclosure, an estate or a tenant
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: after final judgment the clerk sets a public sale 20 to 35 days out unless the lender consents to a longer gap. Homestead owners should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale about leftover funds.
  • Estate: summary administration fits a modest estate, meaning $150,000 or under outside exempt assets, or a death over two years ago.
  • Tenants: month-by-month occupants need 30 days' notice. A tenant who raises any defense besides payment must deposit accrued rent with the court within five days of service.

sections.h2: What to prepare before a Jacksonville buyer visits
sections.html:
• Recorded deed, survey if you have one, and the latest tax bill.
  • Payoff letters, and association paperwork for condos and HOAs.
  • Receipts and permits for the roof, systems and any storm repairs.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers if the house is occupied.
  • For an inherited home, the court order authorizing the sale.

After a contract is signed, the title agent orders title work, collects the payoff letters, prepares the deed and sets up the two witnesses. The clerk records the deed and takes the tax. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, but ask for a written timeline either way.

faqs.q: Does Jacksonville charge a different deed tax?
faqs.a: No. Duval County uses the 70 cents per $100 rate. The revenue department lists only Miami-Dade as different.

faqs.q: When is the Duval homestead deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 each year. Late filing is allowed through early September, tied to the 25th day after proposed-tax notices are mailed in mid-August.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my homestead benefit?
faqs.a: No. The sale resets assessed value to market value for the next roll, and the buyer applies for their own exemption.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant living there?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease. Tenancies by the month end on 30 days' notice, and an unpaid-rent case starts with a three-day written notice.
